evals.name: mixed-quadrant-page
evals.prompt: A draft page 'Getting started with Reactors' opens with 'A reactor is an abstraction over event observers.', walks a newcomer through building a first reactor, then pastes a 40-row table of every attribute and option in the middle of the lesson. Review it and say how to fix it. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Classify the page as a tutorial. Open with the reader's problem and payoff, not an abstract definition. Move the exhaustive option table to a linked reference page; keep the lesson threaded with visible results and let the first success come before theory.
assertions: Classifies the page as a tutorial, with learning as its primary purpose.
Says the opening should state the reader's problem and payoff rather than an abstract product definition.
Recommends moving the exhaustive attribute table to a linked reference page instead of burying it in the lesson.
Says each tutorial step should have a visible result and that deeper theory links to an explanation rather than interrupting the lesson.

evals.name: unsafe-first-path
evals.prompt: Our tutorial's first snippet configures the server with a hardcoded admin password, binds it to 0.0.0.0, and explains four alternative hosting options before the reader sees a result. Critique this against our documentation rules. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: The first path must be the smallest safe configuration that runs: bind to loopback, label development credentials as such, and move host and configuration alternatives into linked how-to guides. The reader reaches a first success before options.
assertions: Says local services bind to loopback in the first path rather than 0.0.0.0.
Says development credentials must be labeled as development credentials.
Moves hosting and configuration alternatives to linked how-to guides rather than showing them in the tutorial.
Says the first working path should be safe to run on a developer machine as written and need no up-front choice among alternatives.

evals.name: reader-feedback-repair
evals.prompt: Prompter logs show readers repeatedly asking 'how do I replay a reducer after changing it?', and an FAQ entry was proposed. The answer exists on a reference page. What do you recommend, and what do you do about issues? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Treat the repeated question as a signal: investigate the page, its entry route or the product behavior behind it. Repair the entry link, wording or example rather than only adding an FAQ. Make an in-scope fix when evidence supports it; otherwise report the gap and suggest an issue, opening one only when asked.
assertions: Treats the repeated question as a signal about the page, its entry route or the product behavior rather than only adding an FAQ entry.
Suggests reducing the report to the page and the sentence-level change the reader expected.
Says to make an in-scope fix when evidence supports it, and otherwise to report the gap.
Says to suggest an issue but open one only when asked.

evals.name: multi-backend-limits
evals.prompt: We are adding a Kotlin backend to a series of 6 pages that currently teach C# only. Two features are unsupported on Kotlin and tracked in issues. How do we handle the limitation text, and what else must we check outside the product's own docs? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Put backend differences once in a 'how the backends differ' table near the start (series index), including unsupported features with their tracking issue, and link it rather than repeating on each page. Search cross-product and site-level pages for single-language claims and series indexes that no longer hold.
assertions: Recommends one backend-differences table on the series index, linked from pages, instead of repeating the limitation on every page.
Includes unsupported features together with their tracking issue in that table.
Says to search pages the product's own checks do not scan, such as cross-product and site-level pages, for single-language claims.
Says to check series indexes whose description, reading order or production claims may no longer hold.

evals.name: ai-drafted-narrative
evals.prompt: I generated a tutorial narrative with a model and want to ship it. What must happen before it ships, and where do I tell the reviewer it was AI-drafted? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: It is a first draft. Revise against source evidence and the voice skill; technical correctness is not established by a style pass. Tell the reviewer in the review request, a PR comment or the commit message, never the PR description, which is published as release notes.
assertions: Treats the AI-drafted narrative as a first draft to be revised against source evidence.
Says a style pass cannot establish technical correctness.
Says to tell the reviewer in the review request, a PR comment or the commit message.
Says not to put the AI-drafted note in the PR description because it is published as the release note.
